## Setting up

#### Q: Which identification tools does RIANA work with?

A: quantms for DDA (RIANA reads its mzTab) and DIA-NN for DIA (its `report.parquet`, with the `[dia]`
extra), both described by an SDRF sample sheet. A Percolator `target.psms.txt` works for a single
run. RIANA does not search spectra itself.

#### Q: Which SDRF columns does RIANA need?

A: At minimum the data file, the labeling time (or, for a calibration, the mixing proportion) and
a condition (`factor value[...]`); biological replicate and precursor enrichment are strongly
recommended. The [Quick Start](install.qmd#the-sdrf-sample-sheet) lists every column RIANA reads.

#### Q: How do I set the labeling sites for my cell type or tissue?

A: Through `--coefficients`, not the label. `--label` only chooses the chemistry (`hw` for heavy
water, the default, or `o18` for ^18^O water); each needs a matching table. For heavy water use
`deberneh_2025_rss` (recommended), `ilchenko_2019`, `commerford_1983` or a cell-culture calibration
(`alamillo_2025_ac16`, `alamillo_2025_ipsc`, `alamillo_2025_cm`); for ^18^O use
`juber_2026_o18_ac16` or `rachdaoui_2009_o18`. You can also pass your own CSV.

#### Q: Where does the precursor enrichment come from?

A: From the SDRF's `characteristics[precursor enrichment]` (e.g. `0.046` for 4.6 % body-water
D~2~O), per experiment. `riana fit --ria` overrides it for every curve; without either, 0.06 is used.


## Fitting

#### Q: Which kinetic models are available?

A: `simple` (one compartment), `guan` (two compartments, with a precursor rate constant) and
`fornasiero` (adds precursor reutilization), plus `calibration` for mixing experiments. At the
protein level, `riana rollup --model "linear simple"` fits a linearized simple model that supports
comparing conditions. See the [Documentation](about.qmd#kinetic-models).

#### Q: How is the fraction of new protein calculated, and can I restrict the isotopomers used?

A: RIANA solves θ against the whole m0–m5 isotopomer envelope with an IsoSpec forward model: θ is
the mixture of the old (natural-abundance) and fully labeled envelopes that best matches the
observed one, given the peptide's number of labeling sites. To use only the leading isotopomers,
for example when heavier channels carry interference, pass `riana fit --fs 3` (m0–m3) or
`--fs auto`. This supersedes the ratio-selection method of Currie et al. (*J Proteome Res* 2025).

#### Q: Why were some of my peptides not fitted?

A: A peptidoform needs enough labeling sites to shift its envelope measurably (`--min-spep`,
default 8 for D~2~O), and enough distinct timepoints (`--depth`, default 3). Timepoints whose θ
falls outside the physical range are dropped as failed solves. The fit log reports how many
peptidoforms the labeling-site gate removed.

#### Q: How do I get half-lives?

A: From the rate constant: $t_{1/2} = \ln(2) / k$, in the units of your labeling time.


## Proteins and comparisons

#### Q: How are protein turnover rates calculated?

A: `riana rollup` keeps peptides unique to one protein that pass the R² gate (R² ≥ 0.8, with a
rescue for flat curves whose k is still well determined), combines their θ within each biological
replicate and timepoint by inverse-variance weighting, and refits k. The median of the peptides' k
(as in our [2022 publication](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mcpro.2022.100252)) is reported alongside.

#### Q: How do I compare turnover between two conditions?

A: `riana rollup --model "linear simple" --reference-condition control`. Each protein gets
`delta_k` = k(test) − k(reference), a p-value and a Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted `delta_k_p_adj`.
With more than two conditions, add `--test-condition` to name the pair. If your runs span several
tissues, split them with `integrate --experiment-column` and the comparison is made within each.

#### Q: My tissues come from the same animals. Can I test whether a condition affects them differently?

A: Yes, with `riana rollup --model "linear simple" --interaction` (or the *Interaction* option on
the desktop app's Protein tab). It fits each protein across tissues with a random effect for the
animal and tests whether the k ratio between conditions differs between tissues. Give each animal
one `characteristics[individual]` ID on all its rows in the SDRF. See the
[Documentation](about.qmd#tissues-of-the-same-animals---interaction).

#### Q: Can RIANA analyze TMT or dimethyl-labeled samples?

A: Yes. TMT/TMTpro channels share one MS1 peak, so RIANA measures the average turnover of a
file's channels; dimethyl channels are separate peaks and are treated as separate samples. Declare
the channels in the SDRF's `comment[label]` column. These designs often use a single labeling time;
RIANA then solves k directly from θ.


## General

#### Q: Is there a graphical interface?

A: `riana gui` (install `riana[gui]`) opens a desktop app with Integrate, Model and Protein tabs. It
runs the same engine as the command line and can display a project's saved results without
recomputing them.

#### Q: How can I contribute to RIANA?

A: Report bugs or open pull requests at <https://github.com/ed-lau/riana/issues>, or contact us at
<edward.lau@cuanschutz.edu>.
